summary: 1936 CCC-erected tower at Cassatt State Forest, Kershaw County; now rebuilt at 40 ft on Billy McIntosh's private land in Sumter County after a late-1990s sale.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with 7'x7' steel cab; formerly 100', reconstructed to 40'
facts.agency: Built for the South Carolina Forestry Commission; owned by Billy McIntosh per NHLR

access.note: Privately owned by Billy McIntosh; the Register describes it as a hunting and wildlife observation spot, but no public access is described

events.note: Erected by Civilian Conservation Corps enlistees at Cassatt State Forest, Kershaw County
SC Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993 (system-wide; not specific to this tower)

evidence.supports: built in 1936 as an Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with 7x7 cab, formerly 100 feet, reconstructed to 40 feet, originally near Cassatt in Kershaw County
evidence.quote: Built in 1936, this Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with 7'x7' steel cab, formerly 100', reconstructed to 40' on the original concrete footings, was originally located near the town of Cassatt in Kershaw County, SC

evidence.supports: 1936 erection of a 100-foot tower by CCC enlistees at Cassatt State Forest
evidence.quote: 1936: A 100-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with 7x7 cab erected by the Civilian Conservation Corps enlistees stationed at the Cassatt State Forest.

evidence.supports: 1947 study of South Carolina's natural resources, quoted by Forest Lookouts, says the state forest was deeded to the Commission in 1935
evidence.quote: Cassatt State Forest was deeded to the State Commission of Forestry by J. R. West on May 28, 1935.

evidence.supports: the state forest is in Kershaw County
evidence.quote: It is located in Kershaw County, contains 462 acres

evidence.supports: the same 1947 study, quoted by Forest Lookouts, says a fire lookout tower was located at the state forest
evidence.quote: A fire lookout tower is located there, but no other forestry management practices have been carried on.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts gives the sale only as 199?? and says it was moved to a private location
evidence.quote: 199??: The tower was sold to a private party, moved and erected at a private location.

evidence.supports: Register says McIntosh purchased the tower from the SC Forestry Commission in the late 1990s and moved it to Sumter County
evidence.quote: The tower was purchased from the SC Forestry Commission by Billy McIntosh in the late 1990s and moved to Sumter County

evidence.supports: the tower was reconditioned and re-erected on McIntosh's property
evidence.quote: reconditioned, and re-erected on Mr. McIntosh

evidence.supports: Register describes the tower as a hunting and wildlife observation spot
evidence.quote: It is used as a hunting and wildlife observation spot.

evidence.supports: magazine dates McIntosh's purchase to the early 2000s
evidence.quote: Shortly after the towers became available for auction in the early 2000s

evidence.supports: two of McIntosh's four towers stand at 40 feet and two at their original 110 feet
evidence.quote: Two of his towers stand at 40 feet, and the other two stand at their original height of 110 feet.

evidence.supports: McIntosh uses the towers to manage and hunt wild game from his property
evidence.quote: uses them as the perfect vantage point from which to manage and hunt wild game from his property

evidence.supports: the SC Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. The Register says the late 1990s, Forest Lookouts gives 199?? and the magazine says the early 2000s. The story reports both and does not choose one.
The Register gives 40 feet after reconstruction, which matches the magazine's count of two 40-foot towers. The magazine does not say which two, so the match is not confirmed for this tower.

notes_for_editor: Build date, CCC erection and the 100-to-40 ft reconstruction come from the Register and Forest Lookouts. The McIntosh purchase year conflicts (late 1990s vs 199?? vs early 2000s). A trail-guide search result (thedirtymule.com, Sumter National Forest Cassatt Fire Tower Ridge Circuit) returned 403 to fetch_text. A WebFetch summary, not a verbatim quote, says the page places the tower's old foundation in Sumter National Forest near Camden and that the tower's own build and move dates are not given. That is unverified and not used in the story; it needs a human check, since the original site may still hold a foundation. No staffing names or notable fires found.
